# YM03: 九洲清晏 Jiuzhou Qingyan, "Nine Continents Clear and Calm"

Malone calls it The Emperor's Private Apartments.

Wave 1 · Yuanming Yuan · 3D: `/reconstruction/3d.html?b=YM03` · Page: `/scenes/YM03/` · Row: `research/buildings/YM03-jiuzhou-qingyan/`

## What it was

九洲清晏 Jiuzhou Qingyan, "Nine Continents Clear and Calm", is the largest of the nine islands round the Back Lake 后湖 Hou Hu and the emperor's residence from Yongzheng to Xianfeng (S05 j80:20b-23b; E1129; S02 pp.77-79, E1153; E1134). Its central axis runs from the Front Lake 前湖 Qian Hu north through three halls: 圆明园殿 Yuanming Yuan Dian (five bays, the garden's name plaque in Kangxi's hand), 奉三无私殿 Fengsan Wusi Dian (seven bays) and 九洲清晏殿 Jiuzhou Qingyan Dian (seven bays in S05; a Yangshi Lei record gives five bays with a three-bay rear porch, S310 rec. 7237), whose plaque is in Yongzheng's hand. East of the last stands 天地一家春 Tiandi Yijia Chun, west 乐安和 Le'anhe (so named as the sleeping hall in 1774) and further west 清晖阁 Qinghui Ge with small buildings round a court (S05 j80:20b-21a, 24a-25b). Malone found the island so built up that there was room for almost no artificial hills (E1153). A fire on 丙申九月二十六日 (1836) burned the three axis halls; Daoguang rebuilt them in under a year to the old form, adding nothing, by his own account (御製重修圓明園三殿記) (E1131, E1132, E1134). 慎德堂 Shende Tang on the west side was built in 1831, the date of Daoguang's essay for it (E1130; S310 rec. 7342); 同道堂 Tongdao Tang had a theatre by 1855 (S43). On 7 October 1860 Swinhoe walked through the audience hall to the emperor's bedroom, where the treaty of 1858 lay on a table (S02 pp.180-181, E2111). Malone, citing Favier, reports that fires broke out during the looting of 6-8 October and burned the emperor's own residence, before the ordered burning (S02 p.183, E1151). The burning of 18-19 October by British troops on Elgin's order followed (E0485). Tongzhi's repair of 1873 renamed several halls (E1135, Q36).

From the inventory row: **built** 最早建筑清晖阁 康熙四十六年 1707 (S42); name under Yongzheng (S42); **changed** 1765 四景 added (S05); 1831 慎德堂, 乐安和/怡情书史 removed (S41; S43); 1836 fire on the central axis, 3 halls rebuilt (S41; S54); 1837 同道堂 (S43); 1855 theatre (S43); Fire on 丙申九月二十六日 (1836). 圓明園殿, 奉三無私 and 九洲清晏 rebuilt to the old form, finished 道光十七年 (1837); 1836 fire; three halls rebuilt by 1837; West line: under Qianlong 乐安和, 怡情书史, 清晖阁; after Daoguang rebuilt as 慎德堂, 同道堂, 湛静斋. South and north landings; 如意桥 to 勤政亲贤 (SE), 南大桥 to 正大光明 (SW), wooden bridges to 镂月开云 (NE) and 茹古涵今 (NW); **destroyed** 1860 (S05, S02, S08, S41, S42, S43, S01, S208, S360, S313).

## The scene itself

### The leaf of 1744, its poem and preface

Leaf 3 of the 1744 album (P0003). Qianlong's preface (S40, E1091; printed in S05 j80:23b-24a) opens: '正大光明直北為㡬餘游息之所棼橑紛接鱗瓦參差前臨巨湖' ('straight north of Zhengda Guangming is the place to rest from affairs; rafters crowd together, scaled tiles stand uneven, and in front lies a great lake'). He compares the islands round the lake to Zou Yan's nine continents ringed by the great ocean, then recalls his father living here, working at maps and books, and binds himself to the same diligence: the poem lists the fear of Heaven and of the people, and sets the fine dishes of the kitchen against the hungry in the ditches. The preface and poem are moral rather than descriptive: they give the dense roofs and the lake in front, not a layout.

### How later sources differ

The 日下旧闻考 Rixia Jiuwen Kao (S05 j80, compiled after 1774) adds what the album lacks: by 1765 the tall pines before 清晖阁 had burned and Qianlong set small buildings round its court, a two-storey 松云楼 Songyun Lou on the high ground of the stone wall, 露香斋 Luxiang Zhai by a rockery, 涵德书屋 Hande Shuwu and the book room 茹古堂 Rugu Tang (j80:24a-25a, E1094). In 1774 Qianlong named the sleeping hall 乐安和; his note says the room he had lived in before was called 随安堂 Sui'an Tang (j80:25a-b, E1099). Jiaqing wrote on 九洲清晏, 奉三无私 and the small studios (E1106-E1114); Daoguang built 慎德堂 in 1831 (E1130) and, after the fire of 1836, rebuilt the three axis halls by 1837 (E1134). The theatre at 同道堂 dates to 1855 at the latest (S43). The plan S01 shows the island after Tongzhi's renaming of 1873 and carries a pasted slip for a later rearrangement (E1135, E1152, Q36); the Yangshi Lei drawings E1156-E1171 record the 慎德堂 interiors and the 九洲清晏 axis at several dates.

Yangshi Lei sheets give three states of the island. Before the fire of 1836: 样004-5 九洲清晏旧样 and 样005-4 慎德堂 fit-out (E1171, E1156). After it: 样005-34 of 1837, an unapproved first round, and 样010-3, the approved rebuilding, which gave the west side of the 九洲清晏 hall the 同道堂 annex instead of a mirror of the east (E1169). Xianfeng: 样007-9-1 of 1855.3 for 圆明园殿 (E1163), 样005-13 and 样005-27-1 of 1855.9, for a three-bay rear porch added to the 九洲清晏 hall that year (E1162), 样004-2-1 for the hall and 同道堂 (E1170), and 样011-3 九洲清晏全样 of 1855.10-12, the latest whole-scene plan found before 1860 (E1161); and the 慎德堂 interior sheets of 1851, 1856 and 1859, one of the 1859 sheets dated only by the site (E1160, E1174, E1164, E1165). The 1874 plan 故1299 (E1166) is Tongzhi's design: same three axes and most old names, but a jade-disc pond with a double-eaved square pavilion between 奉三无私 and 天地一家春, a seven-bay hall north of it, 慎德堂 as five bays under four roofs, 思顺堂 in the west court (S310 rec. 11901). The 1873-74 three-garden plan 样1203 renames 基福堂 to 同顺堂 and 天地一家春 to 承恩堂 (E0532; S310 rec. 7217); the decree of 1873, as quoted in S220, has 思顺堂 for 基福堂 (E1135). S01's labels here (七间殿, 福寿仁恩, ?顺堂, 承恩堂, 同顺堂) are those of the Tongzhi design, which supports Q36.

## Interior and setting

### Interior

Plaques and couplets by hall (S05 j80:21a-23a): 圆明园殿 has Kangxi's 圆明园 plaque, a couplet Yongzheng wrote as a prince ('每對青山緑水㑹心處…') and one by Qianlong; 奉三无私殿 holds Qianlong's copies of the moral instructions of Kangxi and Yongzheng, the plaque 清虚静泰 and a couplet at the throne; 九洲清晏殿 carries Yongzheng's plaque in front and 蔚然深秀 at the back. On the north wall of 清晖阁 hung the painted map of the whole garden of 1737 by Castiglione, 唐岱 Tang Dai, 孙祐 Sun You, 沈源 Shen Yuan, 张万邦 Zhang Wanbang and 丁观鹏 Ding Guanpeng, inscribed 大观 (j80:23a; S02 p.62). In 1860 Swinhoe found, in what he took for the emperor's own rooms, a moderate room with a double-seated throne, chandelier and clocks, two small rooms and a spiral stair to two upper rooms of books whose windows looked down into the hall (E1037); M'Ghee a court about 50 ft square flagged in marble and the only spiral stair, on the left, in the ladies' rooms (E1150). Hérisson's side rooms full of gold, beside the throne hall, are not trusted (S246 pp.315-317, E2441).

### The garden around it

The island faces the Front Lake on the south and the Back Lake on the north (S05 j80:20b, 23b; E1153). Malone found little rockwork and almost no artificial hills on it (E1153). In the west court a long stone wall stood opposite 清晖阁, with tall pines in front that had burned by 1765 and others still standing outside the wall; 露香斋 sat by a rockery with real trees (S05 j80:24a-b). M'Ghee describes the apartments' front on 'another sheet of water' with large planted rockeries (E1150); Wolseley and Swinhoe reached them by a pebbled path round half a pond from behind the audience hall (E1037, E1038). Bridges: 如意桥 Ruyi Qiao on the south-east and 南大桥 Nan Da Qiao on the south-west, 棕亭桥 Zongting Qiao at the north-west corner (S313; S41).

## What survives today

The island keeps its shape between the front and back lakes. An archaeological survey (勘探) report gives the scene about 220 x 120 m, 25,000 m2, with 8,600 m2 of buildings and 656 rooms and gallery bays (S151, opening only); a 紫禁城 article of 2011 gives the island about 234 x 116 m and 21,600 m2 (S313). The page that carries the report says that the foundations of the Tongzhi repair were wrecked in 1900 by bannermen and bandits (S151); who did the damage of 1900 is disputed (Q28). No dig report with hall sizes has been seen; the paywalled report and a 慎德堂 dig record are on the wish list.

## The best views for modellers

For the 1860 state the plan to get is 样011-3 九洲清晏全样 (1855.10-12, NLC; 1207x675 mm, ink, light colour, yellow slips; E1161), with 样005-27-1 (rear porch of 1855) and 样007-9-1 (圆明园殿 measured 1855.3, its slips give bays, depth, column height and platform). For interiors 样008-18 (1859.7) is the latest dated 慎德堂 state found. None of these images could be seen: mhymy shows only the catalogue header and an introduction (where some slip figures are transcribed); the full record is behind a reply wall or payment. The 1874 plans (故1299, 样1203) and the 烫样 are of the Tongzhi repair and must not replace the 1855 sheets.

The 1744 leaf (P0003) is the period colour record of the island's axis before the 1836 fire: grey tile throughout, red columns with green-blue lattice, three main halls rising north from the front lake, stepped covered galleries between them, dense courts east of the axis and pines west. Bays are only roughly countable at the 1920 px copy. The 1745 woodcut (P0089) draws the courts more fully and adds a pyramid-roofed pavilion on the hill at top left; the 1887 page (P0234) is a re-cut of it. The gouache (P0103) recolours roofs yellow and is not evidence for colour. (S08 P0003; S76 P0089; S260 P0234; S77 P0103)

## Gaps and wishlist

For the axis halls S05 gives bays only. The 1855 slips of 样007-9-1, read in the mhymy transcription only, give bays, depth, column height and platform for 圆明园殿 (S310 rec. 11195); for the other halls no depth, roof form, storeys or tiles were found in any text read. The 1855 overall plan E1161 and the interior drawings of 慎德堂 (E1156-E1160) are research-only and their sizes were not read here. 怡情书史, 基福堂, 同道堂 and the 1855 theatre have no Qing text of their own in this round beyond the 1873 renaming (E1135). The S360 compilation of dated records could not be fetched again this round (site timed out).

### Open questions that name it

- **Q4. The pasted slips.** Malone names slips at 九洲清晏 (p.72 caption, p.80 note) and 如意馆, group 40 (p.96 note; App. II). A footnote nearby was first read as being about Qichun: it is not. **None is on this copy at those places.** One slip is seen, at 海晏堂 (Q2). If the flat paper hides a slip, or if the tracing copied only

### Round 18: the detailed model of the axis

The central axis is now a detailed model, `models/YM03-jiuzhou-qingyan/` (its README holds the evidence by part, the iteration log and the joints), with the three named bridges as models of their own (`models/YM03-21-ruyi-qiao/`, `YM03-22-nanda-qiao/`, `YM03-23-zongting-qiao/`). What this round found, beyond the dossier above:
- **The axis re-read on S01** (`models/YM03-jiuzhou-qingyan/plan_readings.csv`): 圆明园殿 five cells with two-cell ear rooms at its ends; a walled yard from the hall to the 前湖 with the landing YMC-023 on its shore; two marks in the first court; 奉三无私殿 drawn wall to wall (S01's cells are uneven; Round 1's box reached 3363 px, the hall ends at 3346) with a front terrace about 20 x 5 m; 九洲清晏殿 drawn in two bands of narrow cells (perhaps the Tongzhi 双卷 design); the walls 22.6 m apart between their inner faces. The seven reads of the axis spread over 2.5 m.
- **The state of 1837-1860 by part:** 圆明园殿 from the slip of 1855 (A), its roof a rolled 硬山 after record 11195 (Q252); 九洲清晏殿 five bays with the 1855 rear porch (A); 同道堂 joined to its west (E1169); every other figure C (圆明园殿's module carried over).
- **The courts** (Q250): S01 kept against the Tongzhi survey's widths and second depth.
- **The leaf P0003** (15 key points in `plate_keypoints.csv`, viewpoint in `photo_viewpoints.csv`, the fit in `plate_fit.csv`, all in this folder): a single camera fits it to 3.79 m rms at the object (median 3.0 m); it paints 九洲清晏殿 as the widest hall (Q251); which halls are the axis is a reading (Q253).
- **Not modelled:** the east of the axis (S01's Tongzhi design, Q255), 慎德堂 and the west road, 清晖阁 and the courts round it, 天地一家春: the kit draws them from their boxes.
